description: We are not chasing what is fashionable. We are chasing what is true, what is provable, and what will still function when the signal drops and no one is coming to help. We build tools that earn their place — not through presentation, but through the unambiguous fact of working correctly under conditions that would break anything less deliberate. This is what we mean by maximum rationalism: not pessimism, not minimalism — just an absolute refusal to pretend that good enough is enough.
summary: SELENA (by team OuroboRust) is a 100% offline autonomous Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) built for deep-space crews facing up to 22-minute one-way Earth communication delays and solar storm blackouts. Running locally as a single native desktop binary (Rust + Tauri v2 + React + Vanilla Three.js) with zero cloud APIs or LLM hallucinations, SELENA unites NASA-STD-3001 physiological triage, 7-slot crew baseline calibration, unit-validated wearable CSV/JSON import, offline EN/RU psychology notes analysis, 365-day cohort correlations, and daily nutrition/hydration countermeasures.
details:
What's happening?
On a Mars transit mission, a signal takes up to 22 minutes to reach Earth — 44 minutes for a round trip — and solar particle events can sever communications entirely. When a crew member deteriorates or cabin ppCO₂ climbs, waiting on Ground Control is not an option.

SELENA is a fully offline autonomous clinical decision-support workstation designed for Day-78+ deep-space crews and flight surgeons. It continuously tracks crew biometrics, sleep, nutrition, hydration, cabin atmosphere, and radiation exposure against published NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 and Volume 2 limits, extracts clinical risk signals from crew notes, and automatically shifts into an isolated shelter protocol during solar communication blackouts.

Because real crews rarely start monitoring from scratch, SELENA can import long-term mission histories and integrate into a flight at any stage — turning raw physiology, environmental telemetry, and crew logs into immediate, NASA-grounded action at the point of care. Every clinical risk evaluation runs in under 2 microseconds (median), with every bit of crew telemetry kept local and independent of Earth.

WHAT IT DOES

• Flight Deck & 3D Habitat: Pairs an interactive habitat view with live crew vitals, cabin environmental gauges (ppCO2, pressure, radiation), and Earth-link signal delay context.

• Clinical Triage & Risk Scoring: Ranks crew members deterministically across cardiovascular, metabolic, sleep, and environmental stressors so subtle drift is caught before acute symptoms appear.

• SPE Blackout Protocol: Switches into an isolated solar-particle-event shelter mode when Earth comms drop, prioritizing radiation dosing, emergency hydration/caloric pacing, and self-contained crew checklists.

• Crew Note Signal Extraction: Scans free-text crew journal entries for clinical symptom, fatigue, stress, and sleep-disruption markers and merges them with quantitative vitals.

• Longitudinal History & Cohort Analytics: Imports multi-month mission archives to reconstruct baselines, track 365-day crew trajectories, and drop into ongoing missions at any point.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Intake: SELENA collects cabin telemetry, biometric logs, sleep and nutrition entries, and short crew notes—either live during flight or by importing long-term mission histories.
2. Thresholding: Each incoming metric is checked against explicit NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 safety limits and OCHMO environmental ceilings.
3. Scoring & Triage: Quantitative trends and extracted note signals feed into deterministic risk models that order the crew by urgency and highlight which parameters are driving the score.
4. Blackout Escalation: When Earth communication lags or cuts out during a solar particle event, the workflow shifts into local shelter guidance with self-contained protocols.

Under the hood, the interface and local computation core exchange typed JSON state snapshots. The core is organized into modular engines—telemetry ingestion, deterministic clinical scoring, note signal extraction, blackout triage, and cohort analytics—accepting structured time-series tables, historical mission archives, and unstructured crew notes.


WHAT WE MEASURED

• Clinical Risk Scoring: 276,025 evaluations/sec (1,986 ns median, 10,710 ns p95, 32,709 ns p99) using deterministic NASA-STD-3001 rules.
• Telemetry Throughput: 125,129 snapshots/sec (7.99 µs/op, 437.9 MB/s JSON serialization throughput).
• Historical Ingestion: 526,891 rows/sec on tabular CSV streams (14.9 MB/s) and 59,388 rows/sec on merged JSON mission histories (10.1 MB/s).
• Note Signal Extraction: 117,413 clinical notes/sec (8.52 µs/note).
• Cohort Analytics: 0.440 ms per full 365-day cohort run (2,270 runs/sec across 365,000 simulated daily records).
• Multi-Core Capacity: 1,871,230 combined operations/sec across 12 threads (600,000 mixed operations in 320.6 ms) and 121,958 ops/sec for crew and countermeasure updates.

ONE LAST NOTE

We genuinely wanted to write an even more detailed breakdown, but decided to leave most of the fun of discovery to you. Perhaps the most important trait of SELENA is its scalability-and with the drive and imagination our team has, we can make it a hundred times better.
